_comment: Questions and checks for scripts/test-review.sh. Each level's `questions` object is sent to Jev verbatim. Every question is one positive judgement a reviewer makes in a second: yes means the thing named is present, never a negation, and each points at a state field in backticks. Criteria examples are deliberately not the calibration fixtures' values, so calibration measures the wording and not recall. A check fires when all its `when` conditions hold: {q, min} holds when the answer is above min, {q, max} when below max, {q, labels, min} when those choice labels' summed probability is above min, and {field, regex[, absent]} is an exact regex over the unit's state (code over Jev wherever the property is checkable). The check's margin is the smallest amount by which its conditions hold; it must clear `band` to report its verdict, and inside the band either way it is reported as Uncertain, never FAIL. `--calibrate` fails any case whose margins sit inside the band in any sample. `model` is the Jev version the conditions were calibrated on; the review asks that version, not an alias.

asserts_mutated_var.instructions: Does `test_body` assert on the value of a shell variable, such as a counter or a flag, that a function in `code_under_test` changes?

criteria.false: The assertions read only `$output`, `$status`, `$lines` or files, or a variable the test set itself that nothing in `code_under_test` changes.

mutation_via_run.instructions: Is the most recent call before `test_body` asserts on a variable that `code_under_test` changes a bats `run` call of the function that changes it?

criteria.true: `run _check_audio` directly followed by `[[ $_launch_errors -eq 1 ]]`: `run` executes in a subshell, so the change never reaches the test.
criteria.false: `_check_audio >/dev/null` directly before the assertion, even when an earlier line ran `run _check_audio` for its output; or `run` wraps only a function that reads the variable; or the test asserts on no such variable.

compares_literal.instructions: Does `test_body` read a value out of a repository file and assert that it equals a fixed literal, such as a count, a sha256, a version or a regex?

criteria.true: `awk` pulls the expected size from `sizes.tsv` and the test asserts `[[ $output == 3 ]]`; or it greps a pin file and asserts the version is `2.1.0`.
criteria.false: The test runs code on an input and asserts on what the code produces, or compares two values the code computed.

feeds_wrong_value.instructions: Does `test_body` hand the code a deliberately wrong value, such as a moved count, a 39-character git sha or a malformed version, and assert that the code rejects it?

criteria.false: Every value in the test is the correct one.

reads_source.instructions: Does `test_body` assert on the text of a production script, patch or data file, read with grep, sed, awk or cat, rather than on what running that code produces?

criteria.false: The test runs the script or patch, on a fixture or a copied bundle, and asserts on its output, exit status or the files it writes; grepping those results counts as running it.

level.instructions: What is the strongest thing `test_body` verifies?

criteria.syntax: Only that `bash -n`, `shellcheck` or `node --check` succeeds on a file, even when the code ran first.
criteria.marker: Only that a string, a patch marker or a file is present, without checking what the code does.
criteria.behaviour: It runs the code and asserts on its output, exit status or the files it leaves.

host_dependent.instructions: Does `test_body` or `setup` depend on the machine it runs on?

criteria.true: It needs network access, a real `gh` or `curl` download, sudo, /dev/input or /dev/uinput, DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY, or reads HOME, XDG_* or _DOCTOR_* without `setup` pointing them at a temporary directory.
criteria.false: Everything it reads is created under a temporary directory, and missing commands are simulated with a shim or a helper such as `_hide_commands`.

checks.title: Side effect asserted through `run`
checks.fix: Call the helper directly (not via `run`) before asserting the counter, as doctor.bats does.

checks.title: Test restates a pinned constant
checks.fix: If it guards behaviour, feed the check a wrong value (a moved count, a 63-char sha) and assert it is rejected, as installer-pin.bats does.

checks.title: Test greps the source instead of running it
checks.fix: Unless it pins deliberate structure, run the script or patch on a fixture and assert its output, exit status and resulting files.

checks.title: Syntax or marker check offered as behaviour
checks.fix: bash -n, shellcheck, node --check and patch markers are the floor. If the change is behavioural, add a test that runs it on a fixture.

checks.title: Depends on the host
checks.fix: Sandbox HOME and XDG_* in setup(), unset ambient variables, and shim network tools on PATH.

reaches_change.instructions: Does a test in `tests` run `function` with input that makes it execute the lines `diff` adds or changes?

criteria.true: `diff` adds a branch for an empty config file and a test passes an empty file; or `diff` rewords a message and a test takes the path that prints it.
criteria.false: Every test takes a path through `function` that skips the lines `diff` adds or changes, or no test runs `function`.

matches_anchor.instructions: Does `function_body` decide whether its input matches using a grep, a regex, a `case` pattern, a `sed` address or an exact string or number comparison?

criteria.false: It only runs a command and passes on its exit status or output.

near_miss_tested.instructions: Does a test in `tests` pass `function` an input that almost matches its anchor and assert that it is rejected?

criteria.true: For `^Exec=`, a line `#Exec=` or `TryExec=`; for a 40-hex sum, a 39-character one; for `== 644`, a file with mode 640.
criteria.false: Every input either clearly matches or is unrelated to the anchor, such as an empty file or a correct value.

stubs_tool.instructions: Does a test in `tests` replace a command that `function` runs with a shell function, a PATH script or a fake binary?

criteria.true: `curl() { echo 200; }`, a script named `jq` on PATH, or pointing a variable such as `TOOL_BIN` at a fake script.
criteria.false: The tests run the real commands on files they create.

failure_tested.instructions: Does a test in `tests` make `function` take a failure branch, such as printing [FAIL] or [WARN], calling `_fail` or `_warn`, or returning non-zero?

criteria.true: A test feeds a bad input and asserts `[[ $output == *'[WARN]'* ]]` or `[[ $status -ne 0 ]]`.
criteria.false: Every test takes the success path.

real_failure_tested.instructions: Does a test in `tests` make `function` take a failure branch while every command `function` runs is the real one, reading input the test created?

criteria.true: The test writes a malformed JSON file and the real `jq` rejects it, driving the [FAIL] branch.
criteria.false: Each failure-branch test gets its failure from a replaced command, or no test takes a failure branch.

pass_on_unchecked.instructions: Can `function_body` reach its [PASS] line or `_pass` call while the value that line reports is empty, non-numeric or was never successfully read?

criteria.false: The value is tested before the pass line (`[[ -n $v ]]`, a regex match, a numeric comparison), or the pass line reports no value read from input.

checks.title: Changed branch not driven by any test
checks.fix: Add a test that takes the changed branch and asserts what it produces.

checks.title: Anchor without a near-miss fixture
checks.fix: Add a fixture one character or one call shape from the anchor that must not match, and confirm loosening the anchor turns a test red.

checks.title: Stub mirrors the production call
checks.fix: Run one FAIL-branch test against the real tool on a real fixture; keep the stub only for the un-fakeable case.

checks.title: Tests never drive the guard to fire
checks.fix: Add a test that drives the guard to fire (the [FAIL], the restore, the mismatch, the rejection), with a stub that returns a failure shape where the real tool cannot.

checks.title: [PASS] on data never read
checks.fix: Guard empty and non-numeric values and every file type before the PASS branch, and add a test feeding each bad shape.

claims_verification.instructions: Does `description` say the author verified the change by hand, for example with a manual run, a mutation test, an inspected bundle or a lint pass?

criteria.true: "Ran it on Fedora 42 and the tray icon shows." or "Reverted the fix and the new test failed."
criteria.false: It describes what changed and why, and names only automated CI results.

checks.title: Claimed verification not committed as a test
checks.fix: Codify the verification the description cites as a committed test.
